data.text: 5... Takeaways from #AZCardinals HC Mike LaFleur's press conference ahead of Camp Day 2: - thought the team was in really good physical shape for where they were at in Day 1. Pleased with how they moved around - on Jacoby needing more time to get caught up: "we'll reassess that day by day. He's a smart dude." Cited language as a big point of learning. Not putting any date on him. Says he's back in offensive meetings and is caught up with playbook compared to other QB's. Likes where he's at from a learning standpoint. - Says he understands offense will be blanketed under similar ones in LA, SF, SEA, etc. but wants to emphasize stars like Trey McBride - on fighting during camp: he told team you don't fight, because you can't fight in a game. Says ramifications can follow and he holds the ultimate authority to make a decision from there. - on the running back room: Says sometimes you have to wait until preseason to see actual progress at the position. When it comes to James Conner, says team doesn't need to have depth chart and they're gonna "do this thing right" and they want to be "responsible" with his return. - In terms of preseason snap counts, he has an idea but still believes it's too early to settle on anything. - On Josh Sweat: He was working with Cardinals "pretty good" this offseason despite being away. Says everybody has been on the same page. He's not worried about Sweat's health. Says no discontent with Sweat. He's "close" - Believes this defense is hungry and was very banged up last year. Excited for healthy unit this year and wanted to emphasize development

data.text: • First Dolphins camp practice is a wrap, some notes: I thought the rookies popped. Jacob Rodriguez got his hans on two passes including a diving PBU on a pass from Ewers to Atwell over the middle. His range in coverage was on display. Caleb Douglas and Kevin Coleman Jr. both had explosives from Willis. Douglas on a short route then a run after the catch where he showed the long speed. Coleman caught a crosser on an absolute bullet from Willis that went for about 25. Douglas also caught a ball on 3rd and 7 right at the sticks with Chris Johnson all over his back, but Douglas plucked it and framed it so Johnson couldn't rake at it. Dulcich had a nice catch and run from Malik, Ben Sims caught some balls from Malik, too. I thought Malik was pretty solid, had one miss on a throw to the outside, had a ball tipped by Rodriguez, but he had good pockets to work from (thought Paul and Jackson did a good job creating deep pockets). Speaking of Johnson, he looks damn good. Explosive out of breaks, doing a little bit of everything. The defense had three splash plays - the biggest a pick six from Willie Gay on a Cam Miller throw outside that he jumped and took back. Michael Taaffe intercepted a ball that Quinn Ewers threw right to him (Bonner also had hands on a Ewers throw but dropped it). David Ojabo punched one out on an Ollie Gordon run. The passing game had some completions, but a handful of balls off frame or over the target. Looked like the first day of camp in that way
